title: Lemon & thyme rapeseed wax candle
subtitle: A UK-grown wax jar candle with a fresh herb and citrus scent
excerpt: A rapeseed wax jar candle scented with lemon essential oil and thyme essential oil. Rapeseed wax is produced from British-grown oilseed rape, a UK-native alternative to soy with similar burn characteristics. The lemon-thyme combination is clean and herbal. Makes one 200 ml jar; burns for around 35 hours.
sourceNotes: Rapeseed (colza) wax candle characteristics: melt point 55-60°C; pour temperature 62-67°C, similar to soy but slightly firmer set. Produced from Brassica napus (oilseed rape) grown in the UK and Europe, making it a local alternative to imported soy. Fragrance load 6-7% of wax weight; EO blends work well. Lemon EO: high limonene content, moderate stability; combine with thyme EO (linalool chemotype for a milder herbal note) for a sustained cold throw. Wick: CD-12 or equivalent for 7 cm jar.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales cleanly. Rapeseed wax is widely available from UK candle suppliers; the burn characteristics are very close to soy so wick sizing guidance for soy transfers directly.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Allow 24 hours cure before burning. The lemon-thyme combination is most vivid in the first 12 months.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Effectively indefinite. The lemon essential oil fades faster than the thyme; the herbal character remains longest.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which melted rapeseed wax is poured into the container, 62-67°C gives a smooth surface without excessive sinkholes as the wax contracts on cooling.
The first burn of a candle, long enough to melt the wax to the full jar edge. Sets the burn pattern for all subsequent uses.

content.text: Lemon and thyme rapeseed wax candle is a clean-scented jar candle made with wax from British-grown oilseed rape. Rapeseed wax burns and behaves very like soy wax, making it a locally sourced alternative for those who prefer a UK supply chain. The lemon and thyme essential oils give a fresh, herbal scent that works well in kitchens and bathrooms. One 200 ml jar; burns for around 35 hours.
